purpose: Codeless USD schema artifacts (plugInfo.json, generatedSchema.usda) for the physx* property namespace.
decisionSummary: Approved decision (option B): do not vendor PhysxSchema. No PhysxSchema codeless artifacts exist at the pinned PhysX SDK revision (tag 106.4-physx-5.5.0), and the separately versioned main-branch schema line (embedded schema version 25.11.1) is not tied to that pinned tag. The project-owned openUsdPhysics schema plugin was expanded instead so every agreed physics domain is representable without any vendored PhysxSchema content.

versionIdentifiers.note: Two independent version identifiers are involved and must not be conflated. '106.4' versions the PhysX SDK repository tag; it is not a PhysxSchema version. The USD schema line carries its own version in schemas/physx/VERSION. There is no such thing as 'PhysxSchema 106.4'.

repositoryCompatibilityBaseline.meaning: The PhysX SDK source revision this repository pins and builds against.

embeddedSchemaVersion.meaning: The version the PhysxSchema USD schema line declares for itself, read from the upstream VERSION file.
embeddedSchemaVersion.relationToTag: Independent of the 106.4-physx-5.5.0 tag. The schema line is versioned and released separately from the SDK tag.

verificationMethod: GitHub REST contents API and raw.githubusercontent.com over HTTPS; every listed URL was fetched and its status recorded.

evidence.observed: Tag resolves directly to commit dd587fedd79836442a4117164ea8c46685453c34.
Repository root at the pinned commit contains no schemas/, no usd/, and no physxSchema/ directory.
No schema tree exists at the pinned commit.
BSD-3-Clause covering the C++ SDK sources that are present in that commit.

upstreamSchemaLine.note: PhysxSchema USD artifacts are published on a separately versioned release line. They are not '106.4' artifacts: 106.4 is an SDK repository tag, while this schema line declares version 25.11.1 in its own VERSION file.
upstreamSchemaLine.hashNote: sha256 values were computed from the raw.githubusercontent.com bytes at the observed commit. The downloaded copies were deleted; no PhysxSchema bytes are stored in this repository.

rejectedSources.reason: The prebuilt wheel carries a custom NVIDIA Omniverse license reference rather than an OSI-approved license, so it is not redistributable by this project.
Distributed under the NVIDIA Omniverse License Agreement; not redistributable by a third-party open-source project.

conclusions: The BSD-3-Clause license of the pinned PhysX SDK commit does not, by association, cover PhysxSchema USD artifacts, because no such artifacts exist in that commit.
The plan's phrase 'PhysxSchema 106.4' names a version that does not exist. 106.4-physx-5.5.0 is an SDK repository tag; the PhysxSchema USD line declares 25.11.1 in schemas/physx/VERSION.
No PhysxSchema plugInfo.json or generatedSchema.usda is vendored into this repository.

Vendoring the main-branch artifacts (embedded schema version 25.11.1) would be license-permissible (BSD-3-Clause) but introduces a schema version that is not tied to the pinned SDK tag. Option B was approved instead, so this is not done.
followUp: If this repository ever adopts the PhysxSchema 25.11.1 schema line, record it as a new approved plan revision and keep the SDK tag and the embedded schema version as two separate fields; never restate the schema version as 106.4.
Foreign physx* properties remain unmodelled by this repository by design. Reading them is a runtime concern, not a schema one.
The managed runtime cannot author a prim's apiSchemas list yet, so generated facades expose Wrap/Has but no Apply. Adding that is tracked separately from this schema work.

approvedDecision.title: Do not vendor mismatched PhysxSchema 25.11.1; expand the project-owned schema instead.
consequences: No PhysxSchema plugInfo.json, generatedSchema.usda, or derived definition is vendored.
Foreign physx* opinions are an optional raw input: read when present, ranked below openUsdPhysics:*, and never required for any domain.

The openUsdPhysics schema plugin covers articulation tendons and mimic joints, particles, PBD materials, fluids and particle cloth, surface deformables, FEM volume deformables, attachments and auto-attachments, collision filters, cooked-data references, vehicles, and character controllers.
Schema semantics are project-owned and independently authored. No NVIDIA schema content, documentation, or licensing text is copied or paraphrased.
